title: Microsoft SSO integration on macOS fails for SAML use cases
body: I am using Firefox 133 on a macOS device that is enrolled through Microsoft Company Portal and shown as compliant. With network.http.microsoft-entra-sso.enabled enabled, visiting either a public or internal application connected to Entra ID through SAML shows a Microsoft login prompt. After credentials and MFA, I am told that I cannot access the resource; the details say the device is unregistered and its identifier is unavailable. On the same machine, an OpenID Connect integration succeeds and Entra's sign-in log recognizes the device as managed and compliant. I expected Company Portal SSO to avoid the prompt and allow the SAML login. I attached screenshots comparing the successful OIDC flow with the failing public and internal SAML applications.

symptoms_visible: On my Company Portal-enrolled and compliant Mac, both public and internal SAML applications prompt for Microsoft credentials and then reject access after MFA.

The error details say 'Device state: Unregistered' and 'Device identifier: Not available', while an OIDC application on the same machine signs in successfully and is recorded as managed and compliant.
N0.label: N0 SAML SSO failure reported

symptoms_visible: After adding <redacted-host> and <redacted-host> to the Microsoft SSO authority list, both SAML applications still show the login prompt and the device-unregistered access error.
N1_x.label: N1_x authority-list change aftermath

symptoms_visible: The SAML applications still prompt and reject my compliant device.
In a fresh-profile recording, the SAML attempt produces no macOSSingleSignOn messages, while the OIDC attempt invokes MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils and receives an ASAuthorizationSingleSignOnCredential.
N2.label: N2 HTTP logging isolates missing SSO invocation

symptoms_visible: Both previously failing SAML applications sign in through SSO in the signed test build, and OIDC still works.
The test-build log now invokes MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils for the tenant /saml2 URL and receives an ASAuthorizationSingleSignOnCredential.
N3.label: N3 signed test build verified

symptoms_visible: After updating Firefox, the previously affected SAML sites now authenticate properly through Entra SSO.
N_terminal.label: terminal SAML SSO working in release

solution.intent: Expand network.microsoft-sso-authority-list with the Microsoft autologon and device-login domains so the existing macOS SSO integration will handle the SAML flow.
solution.concrete_example: Add <redacted-host> and <redacted-host> to network.microsoft-sso-authority-list, then retry both SAML applications.

edges.comment: Reporter c4 on the reporter's Mac: both domains were manually added to the authority-list preference, but the public and internal SAML flows continued to exhibit the same prompt and device-unregistered error.

question_patterns: Could you capture HTTP logs from a fresh profile with nsHttp:5 and macOSSingleSignOn:5 while reproducing the SAML login?
Please record one failing SAML attempt and, if possible, compare it with the working OIDC attempt.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recorded both from a fresh Firefox profile. The SAML login log has no mention of macOSSingleSignOn at all. The OIDC log contains MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils::AddMicrosoftEntraSSO for the authorize URL and later says it got an ASAuthorizationSingleSignOnCredential, with a 200 response and device headers.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The SAML recording already contains MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils::AddMicrosoftEntraSSO for the /saml2 URL and an ASAuthorizationSingleSignOnCredential before the access error appears.
I get the same contrast after another fresh-profile recording, with different redacted tenant and process identifiers.

edges.comment: Participant2 c6 requested private HTTP logging; reporter c8-c9 supplied the reporter's fresh-profile raw comparison. The reporter additionally noted that SAML posts to /TENANT/saml2 without query arguments and independently questioned the source condition requiring a nonempty query; those unprompted observations enter N2.volunteered_info.

question_patterns: Could you try this signed test build against both affected SAML applications and tell me what happens?
Please test the provided build with the same SAML and OIDC cases and share the resulting behavior and log output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Tested. Both SAML2 applications that previously failed now work through SSO. The log invokes MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils for https://<redacted-host>/XXXXXXXX/saml2 and then reports an ASAuthorizationSingleSignOnCredential with a 200 response and device headers. OIDC is still working too; I did not spot a regression.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The signed build still produces the login prompt and device-unregistered error for both SAML applications.
Both SAML applications work in the signed build, but I only captured a log from the internal one.

edges.comment: Participant2 c11-c14 sent a signed candidate build to the reporter; reporter c15 and c17 verified both previously affected SAML applications and supplied raw log output plus the successful-authentication screenshot. This is pre-landing candidate-build measurement, so it does not change the retained system state.

solution.intent: Remove the nonempty query/path gating from the macOS Microsoft Entra SSO activation path so queryless SAML POST endpoints such as /TENANT/saml2 invoke the operating-system SSO API, while retaining authority validation and confirming OIDC still works.
solution.concrete_example: Stop requiring a nonempty URI query before calling MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils on eligible Microsoft authority requests. A SAML POST to https://<redacted-host>/TENANT/saml2 can then obtain the Company Portal credential; invalid URLs can fall through after the operating-system API reports an error. Ship the change only after the affected SAML applications and OIDC have been checked on a build containing it.
solution.inference_hint: The decisive inference is that the nonempty-query condition prevents the macOS SSO hook from running for the queryless /TENANT/saml2 POST. The reporter supplied the contrasting raw logs, endpoint form, and a source-level hypothesis; maintainers accepted the diagnosis, removed the URI check, and validated it through the signed build. Later discussion considered narrower path checks but ended with complete removal of this check.

edges.comment: Reporter c15 verified the candidate before landing. Maintainers c19-c26 reviewed the path/query edge cases and accepted complete removal of the check; reporter c29 subsequently confirmed on the reporter's own system that the previously affected sites worked in the updated release. Uplift and scheduling messages are intentionally not scored.

solution.intent: Fix the macOS Entra SSO request eligibility logic so SAML POST endpoints without query arguments can invoke Company Portal SSO, then have the reporter verify affected SAML applications and OIDC on a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: Inspect the macOS Entra SSO activation condition and remove its requirement for a nonempty query so a tenant /saml2 POST can reach MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils. Provide a test build and verify both affected SAML applications as well as the working OIDC case before declaring resolution.
solution.inference_hint: This is the direct-answer shortcut. The real thread established the diagnosis through authority-list falsification, comparative logging, endpoint inspection, and a signed test build; an agent proposing the correct source-level fix immediately must still request verification rather than claiming success.

edges.comment: Benchmark shortcut from the reporter's opening state to the accepted technical resolution. It skips the reporter's c4 authority-list attempt, c8-c9 logs and source hypothesis, and c15 candidate-build result while preserving the requirement for user verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the macOS Entra SSO path required a nonempty URI query, so a queryless SAML POST to a tenant /saml2 endpoint never invoked MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils, while OIDC authorize URLs with query arguments did.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected contrast: no macOSSingleSignOn messages during the failing SAML attempt, normal SSO credential acquisition during OIDC, and successful SSO invocation for the same /saml2 endpoint in the signed test build.
Must fix the request eligibility logic by removing the nonempty query/path check for eligible Microsoft authority requests, rather than treating the authority-list domains as the solution.
Must not recommend adding <redacted-host> and <redacted-host> to network.microsoft-sso-authority-list as the fix; that persistent change was tried and both SAML failures remained.
Must preserve the working OIDC flow and have the reporter verify both affected SAML applications on a build containing the fix before treating the issue as resolved.
Resolution may be declared only after the reporter's own confirmation that the previously affected sites work in an updated release.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically proficient enterprise user or administrator: understands Entra ID, SAML, OIDC, MDM compliance, Firefox preferences, HTTP logging, and can inspect Firefox source, but explicitly says they are unfamiliar with Firefox internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, analytical, and cooperative; supplies comparisons, logs, endpoint details, screenshots, and source references; tests signed builds promptly and challenges edge-case assumptions constructively.
